front: Name the four duck groups in BC.
back: Puddle ducks, divers, mergansers, sea ducks (85%).

front: Tips up to feed, jumps straight up to fly. Which group?
back: Puddle duck (dabbler) (80%).

front: Dives to feed, patters along the water to take off. Which group?
back: Diver (80%). Exception: the bufflehead can jump straight up.

front: Which diver can jump straight off the water?
back: The bufflehead (80%).

front: Big, broad wings, slow steady beats, loose flocks. Who?
back: Mallard (80%).

front: Slim cross shape, long neck, needle tail. Who?
back: Northern pintail (80%).

front: White patch on the FRONT of the wing in flight. Who?
back: American wigeon (85%).

front: Tiny, low, fast; the whole flock twists as one. Who?
back: Green winged teal (80%).

front: Huge bill held low in flight. Who?
back: Northern shoveler (85%).

front: Long square tail, dark wings, head held up. Who?
back: Wood duck (80%).

front: Wings set far back, big white wing patches, wings whistle. Who?
back: A goldeneye (85%).

front: White stripe along the back of the wing, pale back. Who?
back: Scaup (85%). Lesser: stripe halfway; greater: almost to the tip.

front: Grey wing stripe and a black back. Who?
back: Ring necked duck (85%).

front: Long sloped head, long body, fast, flies in lines or a V. Who?
back: Canvasback (80%).

front: What is the speculum?
back: The coloured patch on the back edge of the wing (80%). It stays the same all season.

front: Blue patch with white bars on both sides?
back: Mallard, hen or drake (85%).

front: The only puddle duck with a white speculum?
back: Gadwall (85%).

front: Green speculum, white trailing edge, slim body?
back: Pintail (85%).

front: Why read the wing before the head in October?
back: Drakes are still in drab eclipse plumage; the wing patch never changes during the season (80%).

front: By when are about 90% of mallard drakes back in colour?
back: Mid November, in a California study (75%).

front: How do you tell a young duck in the hand?
back: Notched tips on tail feathers (75%). In mallards the notch is unreliable from early September (70%).

front: Brown hen, orange and black bill, blue patch?
back: Mallard hen (85%).

front: Brown hen, white patch at the base of the bill?
back: Scaup hen (85%).

front: Dagger bill, sits low, dives near your decoys. Shoot?
back: No. A loon or a grebe: no open season (90%).

front: Slate grey, white chicken bill. Legal?
back: American coot: legal, its own limit of 10 a day (99%).

front: Thin red bill with teeth. Duck or not?
back: Merganser: a duck, counts in your 8 (95%).

front: Daily duck limit and the four restricted species?
back: 8 a day. Inside it: 4 pintail, 4 canvasback, 2 goldeneye (both kinds), 2 harlequin (99%).

front: Duck possession limit?
back: 24, and not more than 12 pintail or canvasback, not more than 6 goldeneye or harlequin (99%).

front: Weigh it: mallard, teal, canvasback.
back: Mallard 1.25 kg, teal 0.4 kg, canvasback 1.35 kg (80%).

front: How many ducks breed in BC, and what share in the Interior?
back: About 1.7 million; about 65% in the Interior (75%).

front: What share of the world's Barrow's goldeneyes breed in the BC Interior?
back: More than 60% (70%).

front: Which way does air move through a bird's lung?
back: One way, pushed by the air sacs, on both in and out breaths (80%).

front: How many breaths move one gulp of air through a bird?
How many air sacs does a bird have?
back: 9: four pairs plus one at the base of the neck (80%).

front: Where does air from the sacs reach besides the lungs?
back: Into hollow bones, including the upper wing bone (80%).

front: Where are a duck's heart and lungs?
back: High and forward, under the wing roots; heart low in the chest behind the keel (75%).

front: What is mostly in a duck's rear belly?
back: Air sacs and gut. Hits there cripple (Tip).

front: How many pellet hits in the vitals kill a duck, with the right size?
back: 1 to 2 (70%, Roster lethality table).

front: What happens to a diver's heart on a long or forced dive?
back: It slows hard to save oxygen, more than in puddle ducks (80%).

front: What anchors the big flight muscles?
back: The keel on the breastbone (75%).

front: What does a duck use instead of teeth?
back: A muscular gizzard with grit (80%).

front: Do ducks have a true crop?
back: No. The gullet stretches to store food (80%).

front: How much grain can a mallard hold in its gullet?
back: Up to about 113 g, a quarter pound (75%).

front: Why do diving ducks have bigger gizzards?
back: They eat hard food like clams and snails (75%).

front: How do ducks stand on ice without freezing?
back: Countercurrent heat exchange: warm blood down beside cool blood back (80%).

front: How much more energy does flying cost than resting?
back: About 12 times (75%).

front: When do ducks fatten?
back: Before fall migration, and again in early winter (75%).

front: Adult mallard yearly survival?
back: About 0.6 to 0.66: 6 in 10 live a year (75%).

front: Oldest known wild mallard?
back: About 27 years (70%).

front: How much of the circle does a mallard see?
back: About 360 degrees (70%). Treat it as seeing everything.

front: How many colour cones do ducks have?
back: Four, including ultraviolet (75%). You have three.

front: Number one thing that flares ducks?
back: Movement, especially a face looking up (75% motion, Tip for the face).

front: How much farther than you can a bird see fine detail?
back: About 2.5 to 3 times (70%).

front: How does a duck judge depth?
back: By moving its head to see from two angles (70%).

front: Mallard hearing range and best spot?
back: About 66 Hz to 7.6 kHz; best near 2 kHz (75%).

front: Where do duck calls sit in pitch?
back: 1 to 3 kHz, their best hearing band (75%).

front: Can ducks smell?
back: Probably yes, but it is barely studied for hunting. Play the wind for the landing (Tip).

front: Which ducks in a sleeping row keep one eye open?
back: The edge birds, eye facing out: about 32% vs 12% for middle birds (75%).

front: When does most migration happen?
back: At night, peaking near midnight (80%).

front: Necks up, still, bunching up. What does it mean?
back: Alert: about to leave. Freeze (Tip).

front: What did GPS mallards do in heavily hunted areas?
back: Avoided hunted ground in shooting hours; about 2 flights a day (80%).

front: How far apart can refuges be and still be linked for mallards?
back: Under about 16 km (10 miles) (80%).

front: How long should you rest a duck spot?
back: A week or more: ducks perceive safety in weeks, not days (75 to 80%).

front: Where do pressured ducks feed?
back: At night, flying out from refuges after dark (80%).

front: When do most mallard hens pair up?
back: Over 80% by early December; courtship peaks Oct to Nov (75%).

front: When does the mallard drake leave the hen?
back: Within days of the start of incubation (70%).

front: Young or adult ducks: which are shot more?
back: Young of the year (80%).

front: Which way do ducks land?
back: Into the wind (80%).

front: Old hand's rule about the roost?
back: Never shoot the roost (opinion).

front: Peak fall passage through the Interior?
back: October (60%).

front: What ends most Interior migration?
back: Freeze up in late November (65%).

front: Mallard clutch and incubation?
back: About 9 eggs (5 to 15); about 28 days (75%).

front: When do ducklings fly?
back: At about 50 to 60 days (70%).

front: How long are ducks flightless in the moult?
back: About 3 to 4 weeks; mallards about 23 to 26 days (75 to 80%).

front: First ducks to leave BC in fall?
back: Blue winged teal, shoveler, pintail: August to early September (75%).

front: Last ducks to leave?
back: Goldeneyes, bufflehead and common mergansers, with the ice (75%).

front: Name 3 changes in October and November.
back: Drakes back in colour, pairs forming, peak passage, freeze up, divers arrive (60 to 75%).

front: A mallard's daily commute?
back: Fields at dawn and late day, water at midday and night (80%).

front: Legal hours for ducks?
back: 30 minutes before sunrise to 30 minutes after sunset (99%).

front: Which weather effect has the strongest evidence for moving ducks?
back: Ice and snow cover (80%).

front: What do ducks do on moonlit, windy evenings?
back: Leave to feed earlier (75%).

front: Cold front with a north wind: hunter lore?
back: New birds; hunt the morning after (65%, lore).

front: Barometer alone and ducks?
back: No good study found (VERIFY).

front: Where do redheads spend midday?
back: Rafted on deep open water; they feed morning and evening (80%).

front: Water depth puddle ducks feed in?
back: Under about 30 cm (75%).

front: Fall foods for ducks?
back: Marsh seeds, pondweed, waste grain; divers add snails and clams (80%).

front: Summer elevation band for breeding ducks?
Winter elevation for ducks?
back: Low valley water below about 700 m (65%).

front: Centre of wood duck abundance in BC?
back: The lower Fraser Valley: Mission (85%).

front: Barrow's goldeneye core range?
back: Dry Interior parkland: your Kamloops country (85%).

front: Hunt Map layers to find duck water?
back: Duck staging and winter waters, plus Wetlands.

front: Hunt Map layers to check you can hunt it?
back: Private land, Parks and protected areas, MU (Management Unit) lines.

front: Can you hunt Vaseux Lake?
back: No: it is a migratory bird sanctuary (99%).

front: Five pond clues?
back: Droppings, feathers, muddy water, lanes in duckweed, webbed tracks (Tip).

front: Describe a duck track.
back: Three forward toes joined by web, tiny hind toe; mallard about 6 cm (60 to 80%).

front: Coot track vs duck track?
back: Coot: lobed toes, no full web (80%).

front: Loud, repeated quack?
back: Mallard hen. The drake is quieter and raspy (75%).

front: Whistling drakes?
back: Wigeon, pintail and teal drakes (70%).

front: Best scouting sign for ducks?
back: The flight line at first and last light (Tip).

front: Duck down, head up, swimming?
back: Shoot again at once, mark it, fetch it (65%; retrieval is the law, 99%).

front: Four ways to hunt ducks?
back: Decoys on water, jump shooting, fields, pass shooting (Tip).

front: Four scouting steps?
back: Map shortlist, watch from far, write it down, permission and wind (Tip).

front: Where is the landing pocket in a J hook?
back: In front of the hide, about 20 to 25 m out (Tip).

front: Why a side wind?
back: Ducks cross in front instead of staring at the hide (Tip).

front: Electronic calls for ducks?
back: Banned. Mouth calls only (97%).

front: Jump shooting in one line?
back: Bend to bend behind cover, rise together, pick one drake (Tip).

front: The five yeses before a shot?
back: Name it, under limit, inside 35 m, safe, can fetch (Tip).

front: Can you shoot from a moving boat with a motor?
back: No. Beached, anchored or tied (99%).

front: Where to aim on a decoying duck?
back: At the bill: head and front half (65%).

front: Minimum pellets in a 76 cm circle: big ducks, teal?
back: 85 to 90 for mallards; 135 to 145 for teal (70%).

front: Best all round steel size for ducks in Roster's table?
back: Steel 3 (70%).

front: Your beginner max range?
back: 35 m (38 yd) (Tip).

front: What must stay on a duck until preserved?
back: A fully feathered wing or the head (99%).

front: Bird flu habits when cleaning?
back: Gloves, outdoors, no eating or drinking, wash up, leave sick birds (75%).

front: USDA safe internal temperature for duck?
Common quoted share of ducks shot but not recovered?
back: About 1 in 5 (65%).
